SPSS-Style Plots

spss-plots.Rmd

Overview

The psych350lab package provides functions to create plots that mimic the appearance of SPSS charts. This includes:

  • A complete ggplot2 theme (theme_SPSS())
  • SPSS color palettes (palette_SPSS(), scale_color_SPSS(), scale_fill_SPSS())
  • Convenience functions for common chart types (spss_histogram(), spss_barchart())

Getting Started 

library(psych350lab)
#> psych350lab v0.1.0 - Functions for Research Methods and Statistical Analysis Lab Course
library(ggplot2)
data(superman)

SPSS Theme

Basic Usage

Apply theme_SPSS() to any ggplot2 plot:

ggplot(superman, aes(x = clark_height_in, y = rt_critics_score)) +
 geom_point(color = "#1192E8", size = 3) +
 labs(x = "Clark Height (inches)", y = "Critics Score") +
 theme_SPSS()
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).

Modern vs Legacy Style

The theme supports two styles:

  • Modern (default): White background, horizontal grid lines, no box border
  • Legacy: Grey background, box border, no grid lines
ggplot(superman, aes(x = clark_height_in, y = rt_critics_score)) +
 geom_point(color = "#3E58AC", size = 3) +
 labs(x = "Clark Height (inches)", y = "Critics Score") +
 theme_SPSS(version = "legacy")
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).

Discrete vs Continuous Scales

Adjust text sizing based on axis type:

ggplot(superman, aes(x = factor(clark_grp), y = rt_critics_score)) +
 geom_boxplot(fill = "#1192E8", alpha = 0.7) +
 labs(x = "Height Group", y = "Critics Score") +
 theme_SPSS(scale.x = "discrete")
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
#> (`stat_boxplot()`).

SPSS Color Palettes

Viewing the Palette 

# Get first 8 colors from modern palette
palette_SPSS(8)
#> [1] "#1192E8" "#005D5D" "#9F1853" "#FA4D56" "#570408" "#198038" "#002D9C"
#> [8] "#EE538B"

# Get legacy palette colors
palette_SPSS(8, version = "legacy")
#> [1] "#3E58AC" "#2EB848" "#D3CE97" "#79287D" "#FBF873" "#EF3338" "#48C2C5"
#> [8] "#CCCCCC"

Using with ggplot2 

ggplot(superman, aes(x = rt_critics_score, y = rt_audience_score, color = factor(type))) +
 geom_point(size = 3) +
 scale_color_SPSS() +
 labs(x = "Critics Score", y = "Audience Score", color = "Type") +
 theme_SPSS()
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).

Fill Scale 

ggplot(superman, aes(x = factor(type), fill = factor(type))) +
 geom_bar() +
 scale_fill_SPSS() +
 labs(x = "Superman Type", y = "Count") +
 theme_SPSS(scale.x = "discrete") +
 theme(legend.position = "none")

SPSS-Style Histogram

The spss_histogram() function creates a histogram with:

  • SPSS blue fill color
  • Optional normal distribution overlay
  • Mean, SD, and N annotation
spss_histogram(superman, "clark_height_in")
#> Warning in ggplot2::annotate("label", x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label =
#> stats_label, : Ignoring unknown parameters: `label.size`

Customization Options 

spss_histogram(
 superman,
 variable = "rt_critics_score",
 bins = 15,
 show_normal = TRUE,
 show_stats = TRUE,
 fill_color = "#005D5D",
 version = "modern"
)
#> Warning in ggplot2::annotate("label", x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label =
#> stats_label, : Ignoring unknown parameters: `label.size`

Without Normal Curve 

spss_histogram(
 superman,
 variable = "rt_audience_score",
 show_normal = FALSE,
 show_stats = TRUE
)
#> Warning in ggplot2::annotate("label", x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label =
#> stats_label, : Ignoring unknown parameters: `label.size`

Legacy Style 

spss_histogram(
 superman,
 variable = "clark_height_in",
 version = "legacy",
 fill_color = "#3E58AC"
)
#> Warning in ggplot2::annotate("label", x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label =
#> stats_label, : Ignoring unknown parameters: `label.size`

SPSS-Style Bar Chart

The spss_barchart() function creates frequency bar charts for categorical variables:

spss_barchart(superman, "clark_grp")

Customization 

spss_barchart(
 superman,
 variable = "type",
 show_counts = TRUE,
 fill_color = "#9F1853",
 version = "modern"
)

Without Count Labels 

spss_barchart(
 superman,
 variable = "tomatometer",
 show_counts = FALSE
)

Saving Plots

Using spss_save_plot() 

# Create a plot
p <- spss_histogram(superman, "clark_height_in")

# Save as PNG
spss_save_plot(p, "histogram.png", width = 6, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)

Using ggplot2’s ggsave()

Since the functions return ggplot2 objects, you can also use ggsave():

p <- spss_histogram(superman, "clark_height_in")
ggsave("histogram.pdf", p, width = 6, height = 4.5)

Building Custom Plots

You can combine theme_SPSS() and the color scales with any ggplot2 code:

Scatter Plot with Regression Line 

ggplot(superman, aes(x = clark_height_in, y = rt_critics_score)) +
 geom_point(color = "#1192E8", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
 geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#FA4D56", se = TRUE, fill = "#FA4D56", alpha = 0.2) +
 labs(
   x = "Clark Height (inches)",
   y = "Critics Score",
   title = "Relationship Between Clark Height and Critics Score"
 ) +
 theme_SPSS()
#> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
#> (`stat_smooth()`).
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).

Grouped Box Plot 

ggplot(superman, aes(x = factor(type), y = rt_critics_score, fill = factor(type))) +
 geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8) +
 scale_fill_SPSS() +
 labs(x = "Superman Type", y = "Critics Score") +
 theme_SPSS(scale.x = "discrete") +
 theme(legend.position = "none")
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
#> (`stat_boxplot()`).

Faceted Plot 

ggplot(superman, aes(x = rt_critics_score)) +
 geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "#1192E8", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
 facet_wrap(~clark_grp) +
 labs(x = "Critics Score", y = "Frequency") +
 theme_SPSS()
#> Warning: Removed 3 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
#> (`stat_bin()`).

Number Formatting

Use number_SPSS() for axis labels without thousands separators (matching SPSS defaults):

# Create data with large numbers
big_data <- data.frame(
 x = c(1000, 5000, 10000, 25000),
 y = c(100, 200, 150, 300)
)

ggplot(big_data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
 geom_point(size = 3, color = "#1192E8") +
 scale_x_continuous(labels = number_SPSS) +
 theme_SPSS()

Theme Parameters Reference

Parameter Description Default
base_size Base font size (pt) 14
base_family Font family “sans”
base_line_size Line width 0.75
base_rect_size Rectangle border width 0.75
version “modern” or “legacy” “modern”
scales “continuous” or “discrete” “continuous”
scale.x Override for x-axis Same as scales
scale.y Override for y-axis Same as scales

Color Palette Reference

Modern Palette (SPSS v24+)

The first 10 colors:

  1. #1192E8 - Blue
  2. #005D5D - Teal
  3. #9F1853 - Magenta
  4. #FA4D56 - Red
  5. #570408 - Dark Red
  6. #198038 - Green
  7. #002D9C - Dark Blue
  8. #EE538B - Pink
  9. #B28600 - Gold
  10. #009D9A - Cyan

Legacy Palette (SPSS <v24)

The first 10 colors:

  1. #3E58AC - Blue
  2. #2EB848 - Green
  3. #D3CE97 - Tan
  4. #79287D - Purple
  5. #FBF873 - Yellow
  6. #EF3338 - Red
  7. #48C2C5 - Cyan
  8. #CCCCCC - Grey
  9. #7AAAD5 - Light Blue
  10. #0A562C - Dark Green
